Simulate gBOIN Trials

Source: R/gboin_simulate.R
gboin_simulate.Rd

Run the gBOIN dose-finding algorithm of Mu et al. (2019) over many simulated trials, for a toxicity outcome with several grades that each carry a score, and return the patients, their grades and the total score at every dose. This is the simulation engine behind sim_gboin, exposed for users who want the raw trial data.

Usage

gboin_simulate(
  target,
  p_grade,
  score,
  n_cohort,
  cohort_size,
  n_trials = 10000,
  start_dose = 1,
  n_earlystop = 18,
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  extrasafe = FALSE,
  offset = 0.05,
  elim_rule = c("posterior", "count"),
  n_earlystop_rule = c("with_stay", "simple"),
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

target

Numeric scalar. Target value of the mean normalized toxicity score, for example 0.313 for a target equivalent toxicity score of 0.47 with a largest score of 1.5. See the details.

p_grade

Numeric matrix. True probability of each toxicity category (rows, from the lowest to the highest) at each dose (columns, in increasing dose order). Every column sums to 1.

score

Numeric vector, one value per row of p_grade. Score of each toxicity category, for example c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5) for grades 0 or 1, 2, 3 and 4. The scores are divided by their maximum.

n_cohort

Integer scalar. Number of cohorts in a trial.

cohort_size

Integer scalar or vector. Number of patients per cohort. A scalar is used for every cohort. A vector shorter than n_cohort is padded with its last element and a longer one is truncated.

n_trials

Integer scalar. Number of trials to simulate. Defaults to 10000.

start_dose

Integer scalar. Dose level for the first cohort. Defaults to 1.

n_earlystop

Integer scalar. The trial stops once this many patients have been treated at the current dose and the design would stay there. Defaults to 18. A value above the maximum sample size switches the rule off.

p_saf

Numeric scalar. Highest mean score deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.6 * target.

p_tox

Numeric scalar. Lowest mean score deemed overly toxic. Defaults to 1.4 * target.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. Posterior probability cutoff for dose elimination. Defaults to 0.95.

extrasafe

Logical scalar. Apply the stricter safety stopping rule at the lowest dose. Defaults to FALSE.

offset

Numeric scalar between 0 and 0.5. Amount by which cutoff_eli is relaxed for the safety stopping rule. Defaults to 0.05.

elim_rule

Character scalar, either "posterior" or "count". How a dose is eliminated. Under "posterior", the default and the rule of the article, the posterior probability is evaluated at the total score. Under "count" the dose is eliminated when the total score reaches the elimination boundary of the number of DLTs of boin_boundary, a whole number, as in the 'UnifiedDoseFinding' package. See the details.

n_earlystop_rule

Character scalar, either "with_stay" or "simple". Under "with_stay" the trial stops at n_earlystop only when the design would remain at the current dose. Under "simple" it stops as soon as the threshold is reached.

seed

Integer scalar or NULL. Random seed. When NULL the current state of the random number generator is used. The state of the calling session is restored on exit. Defaults to 123.

Value

An object of class c("gboin_trials", "boin_trials"), which is a list with components

n_pts

Integer matrix, n_trials by number of doses, of patients treated.

n_tox

Numeric matrix of the same shape: the total of the normalized scores of the patients treated at each dose (the total of the scores as given, divided by the largest score), which takes the place of the number of DLTs.

n_grade

Integer array, n_trials by doses by toxicity categories, of the patients in each category. The categories take the row names of p_grade when every row has one, and G1, G2, ... otherwise.

eliminated

Logical matrix marking doses eliminated during the trial.

cohorts_used

Integer vector of cohorts completed in each trial.

stop_reason

Character vector giving why each trial ended.

lambda_e, lambda_d

The escalation and de-escalation boundaries of the mean score.

design

The name of the design, "gBOIN".

settings

List of the design parameters, with the true mean normalized score of each dose in p_true.

Details

The gBOIN design generalizes the BOIN design to toxicity outcomes from the exponential family. This function covers the quasi-Bernoulli outcome: every toxicity category carries a score, such as the equivalent toxicity score (ETS) of Yuan et al. (2007), and the scores divided by their maximum, which lie between 0 and 1, are treated like fractional DLTs. With x the total normalized score of the n patients treated at the current dose, the design

  • escalates when x / n <= lambda_e,

  • de-escalates when x / n >= lambda_d,

  • stays otherwise,

where lambda_e and lambda_d are the BOIN boundaries of boin_lambda for target, p_saf and p_tox; they are the optimal boundaries for the quasi-Bernoulli outcome as well (Theorem 1 of the article). A dose with at least three patients is eliminated, together with every higher dose, when the posterior probability that its mean score exceeds target, from the distribution Beta(x + 1, n - x + 1), is above cutoff_eli; the next cohort is then treated at the dose below, and the trial stops when the lowest dose is eliminated.

target, p_saf and p_tox are on the normalized scale. The article computes its boundaries for the ETS example (0.373 and 0.566) from the unnormalized target of 0.47; on the normalized scale the target is 0.47 / 1.5 = 0.313 and the boundaries, multiplied by 1.5, are 0.371 and 0.562.

The reference implementation in the 'UnifiedDoseFinding' package applies the elimination boundary of the number of DLTs, a whole number, to the total score, which eliminates a dose a little later than the posterior probability evaluated at the total score itself, the rule the article describes. elim_rule = "count" gives the rule of the package; it is meant for comparisons with it. For whole numbers of DLTs the two rules are the same.

One uniform variate is drawn per patient, in enrollment order: the patient falls in the highest category for which the probability of that category or a higher one exceeds the variate. A cohort cut short by the maximum sample size still draws a full cohort's worth. With two categories of scores 0 and 1 the trials are therefore, for the same seed, those of boin_simulate without titration.

The total normalized score of a dose is the total of the scores as given, divided once by the largest score, as in gboin_et_simulate. With scores that are binary fractions, such as 0, 0.5, 1 and 1.5, the total of the scores as given is exact, so that the same patients give the same total, and the same decision, on every platform.

Possible values of stop_reason are "lowest_dose_eliminated", "lowest_dose_too_toxic", "n_earlystop", "max_sample_size" and "max_cohorts".

References

Mu, R., Yuan, Y., Xu, J., Mandrekar, S. J. and Yin, J. (2019). gBOIN: a unified model-assisted phase I trial design accounting for toxicity grades, and binary or continuous end points. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series C, 68, 289-308. doi:10.1111/rssc.12263

Yuan, Z., Chappell, R. and Bailey, H. (2007). The continual reassessment method for multiple toxicity grades: a Bayesian quasi-likelihood approach. Biometrics, 63, 173-179.

See also

sim_gboin, gboin_select_mtd, boin_lambda

Examples

# Scenario 1 of Mu et al. (2019): grades 0 or 1, 2, 3 and 4 at six doses
p_grade <- rbind(
  c(0.83, 0.75, 0.62, 0.51, 0.34, 0.19),
  c(0.12, 0.15, 0.18, 0.19, 0.16, 0.11),
  c(0.04, 0.07, 0.11, 0.14, 0.15, 0.11),
  c(0.01, 0.03, 0.09, 0.16, 0.35, 0.59)
)
trials <- gboin_simulate(
  target = 0.47 / 1.5,
  p_grade = p_grade,
  score = c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5),
  n_cohort = 10,
  cohort_size = 3,
  n_trials = 200,
  seed = 123
)
trials
#> Simulated gBOIN trials
#>   trials          : 200
#>   doses           : 6
#>   target score    : 0.3133333
#>   cohorts         : 10 of size 3
#>   max sample size : 30
#> 
#> Average per trial:
#>                   DL1  DL2  DL3  DL4  DL5  DL6
#> Patients treated 3.42 5.20 8.85 8.87 2.79 0.33
#> Toxicity score   0.24 0.68 1.95 2.83 1.39 0.26
#> 
#> Stopping reason (%):
#> 
#> max_sample_size     n_earlystop 
#>              87              13 

# Average number of patients of each grade at each dose
apply(trials$n_grade, c(3, 2), mean)
#>      DL1   DL2   DL3   DL4   DL5   DL6
#> G1 2.845 3.910 5.545 4.425 0.990 0.035
#> G2 0.430 0.740 1.565 1.830 0.395 0.035
#> G3 0.135 0.375 0.950 1.165 0.435 0.035
#> G4 0.010 0.180 0.790 1.445 0.970 0.225
